gen-dafont-quantum-gf-biryani: Clean is the first impression here, with Quantum spacing its letters loosely and leaving its curves open. And Biryani follows with large-eyed e shapes and no stroke modulation, keeping its small counters clear.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-blinker: Wide letterfit with generous breathing room is what defines Quantum, a display face with compressed ascenders and open curves. Blinker, a plain sans, then fills the line with tall lowercase.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-carrois-gothic: Carrois Gothic reads modern and businesslike, its high-set lowercase and generous curve openings keeping text easy to follow. Carrois Gothic sits under Quantum, whose rod-stock strokes and loose spacing make the headline feel sharp.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-carrois-gothic-sc: Quantum's thin-looking letters, all with the same thickness throughout and spaced loosely, are what you notice first. Carrois Gothic SC follows with open curve endings and capitals that barely rise above the lowercase.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-chivo: Quantum has a marker-drawn plainness in every character, loosely spaced and tidy, with ascenders held short. Chivo underneath packs its lowercase up toward the caps and lets daylight through each curve.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-chocolate-classica: Quantum does the tube-like, constant-width tech look best, with loose spacing and open mouths. But Chocolate Classical Sans does the reading work, its sizable lowercase drawn with a broad-nibbed stroke that never closes up.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-comme: Modern through and through, Quantum cuts its letters like stencils. Quantum does the crisp, uniform-width headline look best, while Comme, a plain sans, handles smooth reading with lowercase that fills most of its height.
